content:
We have search results list of templates. Need to find the one that matches our target molecule and reproduces the described reaction: aromatic amine attacks phenylsulfonyl chloride, forming sulfonamide. The forward reaction: Ar-NH2 + ClSO2-Ph -> Ar-NH-SO2-Ph + HCl (base deprotonates). So retrosynthetic step: break N-S bond, form sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-Ph) and aromatic amine (Ar-NH2). The template should have functional group formed sulfonamides and bond broken S-Cl (in forward). The search gave several templates. Need to pick the appropriate one that when applied to our molecule yields precursors: the sulfonyl chloride (phenylsulfonyl chloride) and the aromatic amine (the aryl amine part). Our target molecule is complex: O=S(NC1=CC(N2CCN(C(OC(C)(C)C)=O)CC2)=C3C(CCC4(CCC4)O3)=C1)(C5=C(F)C=CC=C5)=O

Let's decode: It's a sulfonamide where the sulfonyl group attached to aromatic ring (C5=...F) and also attached to N of an aniline that is part of a heterocycle? Actually N attached to aromatic ring C1=... So the sulfonyl group is attached to N (forming sulfonamide) and also attached to phenyl with F. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be phenylsulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-PhF). The amine precursor would be the aromatic amine: NC1=CC(...). So we need a template that splits N-S bond and adds Cl to S.

Look at first result (reaction_id 20810). The retro_smarts_template: '[C:5]-[#8:6]-[c:7]1:[c:8]:[c:9]:[c:10](-[NH;D2;+0:11]-[S;H0;D4;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:2])(=[O;D1;H0:3])-[c:4]):[c:12]:[c:13]:1>>Cl-[S;H0;D4;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:2])(=[O;D1;H0:3])-[c:4].[C:5]-[#8:6]-[c:7]1:[c:8]:[c:9]:[c:10](-[NH2;D1;+0:11]):[c:12]:[c:13]:1'

This seems to split sulfonamide into sulfonyl chloride and aniline (with a phenoxy group?). The product side (retro) is sulfonamide; reactants are sulfonyl chloride and aniline with OH? Actually the first part: Cl-[S...]-[c:4] (sulfonyl chloride attached to aromatic carbon). Second part: [C:5]-[#8:6]-[c:7]... which is a phenoxy? It includes C-O-aryl with NH2. That seems not exactly our case but could be generic.

Our target has sulfonyl attached to aromatic ring (c5=...), and N attached to aromatic heterocycle (maybe an aniline). The template likely matches.

We need to return mapped_rxn and template_id (the integer ID used to search). The search result includes 'template_id'? Actually each entry has 'reaction_id' and 'template_hash', but not template_id. The tool likely returns template_id as part of each dict? The description says returns list of templates each with details, maybe includes 'template_id' field. In result we see 'reaction_id', 'template_hash', 'retro_smarts_template', 'canonical_smarts_template', 'mapped_rxn', etc. No explicit template_id. Possibly template_id is the 'reaction_id'? But the prompt says "template_id (the one used to search the database not the hash) as an integer". So likely template_id corresponds to 'reaction_id' (or maybe a separate field). We'll assume reaction_id is template_id.

We need to verify which template matches our molecule. Could test with check_smiles_reaction_template_matching for each candidate. Let's try first candidate template_id 20810.
